messages.author: 7e980a045f69e09d
messages.subject: Plotting shape change
parts:
Hello everyone, I want to create a different deformation grids for each species I'm examining; how the average of each species changes from the overall average (all species combined). I would like to interpret the shape changes and describe certain areas as wider, longer, etc. I've utilized some code I found here, but seem to be getting stuck. I've used the plethodon dataset as an example so it's clear what it being done.

When I utilize code I found on this group's page I seem to only get a flat grid with no warping. I've attached a photo of the grid. I get a grid with no warping using my data as well. My first thought it that there is so little change that I'm not getting warping in the grid.

data(plethodon) 
Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethodon$land)   
coords.jord <- Y.gpa$coords[,,plethodon$species=="Jord"]
mean.jord <- mshape(coords.jord)
grand.mean <- mshape(Y.gpa$coords)
plotRefToTarget(grand.mean, mean.jord, method="TPS") 

That's my first problem.  My second problem is I want to add vector arrows as well, but I can't seem to figure out how to. I just get arrows pointing back at my points.

arrows(grand.mean[,1],grand.mean[,2],mean.jord[,1],mean.jord[,2],length=0.1,lwd=2)


I also have another question about grid interpretation. If I have species A as reference and species B as target, can I use that grid to interpret shape changes, like species B is wider than species A?

I've been trying to find help on this for a while and keep getting stuck. Sorry for the basic questions, I'm newer to R and still learning.

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Plotting shape change
parts:
Lindsay,

the example code you sent does what it should, and produces "deformed" grids. Maybe they are not too visible because the amount of shape change is small. Try exaggerating it a bit by using:

plotRefToTarget(grand.mean, mean.jord, method="TPS", mag=5)

You can make a vectors plot by using:

 plotRefToTarget(grand.mean, mean.jord, method="vector", mag=5)

If you want to have both the grid and the vectors, you will have to do that by hand, as geomorph does not provide that plotting option. I believe the Practical Companion Mimi Zelditch sent out some days ago includes an example on that, you can find the post here: plotRefToTarget(grand.mean, mean.jord, method="TPS", mag=5)

As for interpretation, it sounds like you have got it right, if what you are seeing are arrows making the structure wider as you move from A to B.

Hope this helps,
Antigoni

messages.author: 2fc03d53bc863e8d
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Plotting shape change
parts:
To add to what Antigoni wrote: the default for the method="TPS" is to show the landmarks of the target form, and you drew the vectors from the reference to the target; because the change is so slight, the arrowheads overlap the landmarks. If you exaggerate the change by 5, you will also need to lengthen the arrows, so you'd need to calculate the coordinates for the new target. If you call the target for the exaggerated change "jord.exag", that would be
jord.exag=grand.mean+5*(mean.jord-grand.mean)

When you look at the result, you can decide whether to show the landmarks where the arrows point, or at the base of the arrow so the arrows are pointing away from them to the landmarks of the target. It you'd prefer the second, add UseRefPts=T to the argument for the deformed grid).
We have a chapter on graphics in the revised Practical Companion, but I don't think that we discussed how to get the coordinates of the target form for a magnified change.
